topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.211, may an examination be used to satisfy any part of a managing broker's continuing education requirement for renewal?
choice_a: No -- examinations shall not be required to fulfill any part of the continuing education requirement
choice_b: Yes, but only for the fair housing portion of the requirement
choice_c: Yes, an exam may substitute for up to half of the required hours
choice_d: Only if the licensee's continuing education hours were completed more than 24 months before renewal
explanation: RCW 18.85.211 expressly states that examinations shall not be required to fulfill any part of the continuing education requirement -- renewal CE is satisfied entirely through completed clock hours of instruction, not testing.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.211, who has the authority to place restrictions on the number of distance education course hours that may be counted toward a managing broker's renewal continuing education?
choice_a: The director
choice_b: The individual course provider only
choice_c: The designated broker of the licensee's firm
choice_d: The real estate licensing examination board
explanation: RCW 18.85.211 authorizes the director to restrict the use of distance education course hours toward the continuing education requirement, giving the director discretion over how much online or correspondence instruction may count.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.265, when does a real estate license become "inactive"?
choice_a: At any time it is delivered to the director
choice_b: Automatically 30 days after the renewal deadline passes
choice_c: Only when the licensee formally requests a hearing
choice_d: Automatically upon completion of a 30 clock hour course
explanation: RCW 18.85.265 provides that any license not otherwise revoked is deemed "inactive" at any time it is delivered to the director -- inactive status is a voluntary surrender of the physical license, distinct from expiration or disciplinary cancellation.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.265, what is a managing broker prohibited from doing while their license is inactive?
choice_a: Conducting real estate brokerage services
choice_b: Renewing the inactive license
choice_c: Applying to reactivate the license
choice_d: Retaining the license number for future use
explanation: RCW 18.85.265 states the holder of an inactive license is prohibited from conducting real estate brokerage services until the license is reissued to active status.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.265, if a managing broker's license has been inactive for more than three years, what must the holder show before applying for active status?
choice_a: Proof of successfully completing a 30 clock hour real estate course
choice_b: Proof of successfully completing the full 90-hour qualifying education again
choice_c: A new passing score on the managing broker licensing examination
choice_d: A letter of good standing from their most recent designated broker
explanation: RCW 18.85.265 requires a holder whose license has been inactive for more than three years to show proof of successfully completing a thirty clock hour course in real estate before applying to reactivate to active status.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.265, within what window before applying for active status must the 30 clock hour course be completed by a licensee whose license has been inactive more than three years?
choice_a: Within one year before the application
choice_b: Within six months before the application
choice_c: Within five years before the application
choice_d: At any time before the application, with no time limit
explanation: RCW 18.85.265 requires the 30 clock hour course to have been completed within one year before the application for active status -- older coursework does not satisfy the reactivation requirement.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under RCW 18.85.265, which licensees are exempt from the 30 clock hour course otherwise required to reactivate a license that has been inactive for more than three years?
choice_a: Holders employed by the state and conducting real estate transactions on behalf of the state
choice_b: Holders who are also licensed attorneys
choice_c: Holders who were inactive for a documented medical reason
choice_d: Holders who previously held a designated broker role
explanation: RCW 18.85.265 exempts holders employed by the state and conducting real estate transactions on behalf of the state from the 30 clock hour reactivation course requirement.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: How does reactivating an inactive license under RCW 18.85.265 differ from reinstating a canceled or expired managing broker license through the Department of Licensing?
choice_a: Reactivating an inactive license is governed by a 3-year/30-hour-course threshold under RCW 18.85.265, while reinstating a canceled license follows the department's separate 2-year/3-year timeline and 60-clock-hour coursework with a $100 penalty fine
choice_b: They are the same process described in two different documents
choice_c: Reactivation always requires retaking the licensing examination, while reinstatement never does
choice_d: Reinstatement applies only to inactive licenses, while reactivation applies only to canceled licenses
explanation: Inactive status (RCW 18.85.265) is a voluntary surrender of an otherwise-valid license, reactivated on a 3-year/30-clock-hour-course threshold; a canceled or expired license instead follows the department's reinstatement rules -- eligible within 2 years of cancellation with 60 clock hours (30 in Real Estate Law) and a $100 penalty fine, with a brand-new application required once expired more than 3 years.
source_note: RCW 18.85.265; DOL: Renew or reinstate your license - Real estate managing brokers

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125, what must the designated broker provide to the department within five business days of closing a real estate firm?
choice_a: A closing firm affidavit
choice_b: A notarized letter of resignation
choice_c: A final trust account bank statement only
choice_d: A list of all licensees terminated from the firm
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125 requires the designated broker to provide the department with a closing firm affidavit within five business days of closing the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125, within five business days of firm closure, what must the designated broker ensure regarding brokerage services contracts?
choice_a: That they are either terminated or transferred to another licensed real estate firm with the parties' written authorization
choice_b: That they are automatically voided without any party notification
choice_c: That they are filed with the county recorder's office
choice_d: That they are renegotiated at the closing firm's discretion
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125 requires that, within five business days, all brokerage services contracts be either terminated or transferred to another licensed real estate firm, and a transfer requires the parties' written authorization.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125, what ongoing trust account practice must a designated broker maintain so the firm is prepared for an orderly closure if it occurs?
choice_a: Current and accurate monthly reconciliation of trust bank accounts with up-to-date monthly trial balances
choice_b: An annual, rather than monthly, trust account audit
choice_c: A trust account balance of at least $10,000 at all times
choice_d: Quarterly reporting of trust balances directly to each client
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125 requires designated brokers to keep monthly reconciliations of trust bank accounts current and accurate, along with up-to-date monthly trial balances showing accounts in balance, as an ongoing safeguard rather than a closure-only task.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125, besides trust account reconciliation, what written materials must a designated broker maintain addressing trust account handling and the safeguarding of customer or client funds?
choice_a: Written policies covering trust account handling and safeguarding of customer/client funds
choice_b: A signed indemnification agreement with the firm's bank
choice_c: A public disclosure statement posted in the firm's lobby
choice_d: Written policies are not required as long as reconciliations are current
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125 requires designated brokers to maintain written policies addressing trust account handling and the safeguarding of customer and client funds, independent of the reconciliation requirement.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125, what must a designated broker maintain regarding managing brokers and branch managers to whom supervisory duties have been delegated?
choice_a: Delegated authority agreements
choice_b: Annual performance reviews filed with the department
choice_c: Separate errors-and-omissions insurance policies for each delegate
choice_d: Notarized power-of-attorney forms
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125 requires designated brokers to maintain delegated authority agreements for managing brokers and branch managers, documenting the scope of supervisory authority delegated within the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, what is the minimum period a real estate firm must retain its required records, available for inspection by the director?
choice_a: A minimum of three years
choice_b: A minimum of one year
choice_c: A minimum of five years
choice_d: A minimum of seven years
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110 requires that all required real estate records be retained and available for inspection by the director or the director's authorized representative for a minimum of three years.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what must a firm's transaction folder contain for each real estate or business opportunity transaction?
choice_a: All agreements, receipts, contracts, documents, leases, closing statements, and material correspondence
choice_b: Only the final signed purchase and sale agreement
choice_c: Only documents that were notarized
choice_d: Only correspondence exchanged after mutual acceptance
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires the transaction folder to contain all agreements, receipts, contracts, documents, leases, closing statements, and material correspondence related to the transaction -- not merely the final signed contract.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, where may transactions that have been closed for at least one year be stored?
choice_a: At one central facility located in Washington, provided records remain readily retrievable on demand
choice_b: At any facility worldwide, with no retrieval timeframe specified
choice_c: Only at the firm's original licensed office -- off-site storage is never permitted
choice_d: At the designated broker's personal residence, regardless of location
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110 permits transactions closed for at least one year to be maintained at one central facility located in Washington, so long as the records are readily retrievable on demand and a transaction listing is maintained at the firm's licensed office.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, when a firm stores records electronically or on a remote device, what must the firm maintain at the licensed office to support that storage?
choice_a: Functioning equipment and a storage system indexed for immediate retrieval of all documents
choice_b: A dedicated server room accessible only to the designated broker
choice_c: Paper backups of every electronically stored document
choice_d: A notarized certification renewed annually with the department
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110 requires that when records are stored electronically or remotely, the firm maintain functioning equipment at the licensed office and keep the storage system indexed to allow immediate retrieval, viewing, and printing of all documents.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(7), within how many business days of mutual acceptance must a managing broker deliver transaction documents and brokerage service contracts to the designated broker or delegated managing broker?
choice_a: Two business days
choice_b: Five business days
choice_c: Ten business days
choice_d: Same-day delivery is required
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(7) requires a managing broker to deliver transaction documents and brokerage service contracts to the designated broker or delegated managing broker within two business days of mutual acceptance, ensuring the firm's records stay current for ongoing supervision and any eventual closure.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, how must a firm's trust bank accounts, deposit slips, checks, and signature cards be designated?
choice_a: As trust accounts in the firm's licensed name
choice_b: As trust accounts in the designated broker's personal name
choice_c: As general operating accounts, with trust status noted only internally
choice_d: As trust accounts in the name of the department of licensing
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 requires trust bank accounts, deposit slips, checks, and signature cards to be designated as trust accounts in the firm's licensed name, keeping client funds clearly separated from the firm's own operating funds.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, trust funds of $10,000 or less must be deposited into what type of account?
choice_a: A pooled interest-bearing trust account identified as the housing trust fund account
choice_b: A non-interest-bearing checking account chosen by the depositing party
choice_c: A separate interest-bearing account for each individual client, regardless of amount
choice_d: The firm's general operating account, temporarily flagged as restricted
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 requires trust funds of $10,000 or less to be deposited into a pooled interest-bearing trust account identified as the housing trust fund account, rather than a separate account for each client.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, what must a licensee do in writing when a party deposits more than $10,000 in trust funds?
choice_a: Disclose to that party their option between a separate interest-bearing account with interest paid to them, or the pooled housing trust fund account
choice_b: Automatically place the funds in the firm's general operating account
choice_c: Refuse the deposit and require it be split into amounts of $10,000 or less
choice_d: Notify the department of licensing before accepting any portion of the deposit
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 requires the licensee to disclose in writing to a party depositing more than $10,000 that the party has a choice between a separate interest-bearing account (with interest paid to that party) or use of the pooled housing trust fund account.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, may a firm disburse funds from its real estate trust bank account before closing of the transaction?
choice_a: No, not without a written release from both the purchaser and the seller
choice_b: Yes, at any time the designated broker deems appropriate
choice_c: Yes, but only for amounts under $500
choice_d: Yes, provided the department of licensing is notified in advance
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 prohibits disbursements from the real estate trust bank account in advance of closing (or before a purchase and sale agreement condition is met) without a written release from both the purchaser and the seller.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, when must a separate commission check be drawn on the real estate trust bank account, payable to the firm as licensed?
choice_a: After the final closing of the real estate or business opportunity transaction
choice_b: As soon as mutual acceptance occurs, before closing
choice_c: At the start of each calendar month, regardless of transaction status
choice_d: Only after the firm formally closes its business
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 requires that a separate check be drawn on the real estate trust bank account, payable to the firm as licensed, for each commission earned, only after the final closing of the transaction -- commissions cannot be drawn against trust funds beforehand.

topic: WA Managing Broker: License Renewal, Continuing Education & Firm Closure
question: Under WAC 308-124E-110, if a party other than the firm holds earnest money for a transaction, what must the licensee obtain and retain?
choice_a: A dated receipt for the earnest money
choice_b: A surety bond covering the full earnest money amount
choice_c: Written approval from the department of licensing
choice_d: Nothing, since the firm bears no responsibility once a third party holds the funds
explanation: WAC 308-124E-110 requires that when a party other than the firm holds earnest money, the licensee must obtain and retain a dated receipt documenting the deposit.
